treatment: Total mastectomy without axillary dissection vs radical mastectomy
population: 1,665 women with operable breast cancer; clinically node-negative and node-positive cohorts
nnt: Not applicable; no significant survival advantage
relativeEffect: 1.03 for total mastectomy vs radical mastectomy in node-negative patients
benefitText: At 25 years, overall survival among clinically node-negative women was 26% after total mastectomy alone versus 25% after radical mastectomy; HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.87–1.23). There was no significant survival difference. Total mastectomy plus radiation also showed no survival advantage. The major difference was better locoregional control with radiation, not survival.
nnH: Not quantifiable from the primary endpoint
clinicalQuestion: Does radical mastectomy improve long-term survival compared with less extensive breast and axillary surgery in operable breast cancer?
refs: Fisher B, et al. N Engl J Med. 2002;347:567–575.

treatment: Mastectomy + postmastectomy RT + systemic therapy vs mastectomy + systemic therapy
population: 1,708 premenopausal women with high-risk stage II/III breast cancer
benefitText: DBCG 82b increased 10-year overall survival from 45% to 54%, an absolute improvement of 9 percentage points (NNT 12). Ten-year locoregional recurrence fell from 32% to 9%, an absolute reduction of 23 points (NNT 5). NNT for OS is based on 10-year survival.
nnH: Not quantifiable from the selected long-term endpoint
clinicalQuestion: Does postmastectomy radiotherapy improve outcomes in high-risk premenopausal stage II/III breast cancer?
refs: Overgaard M, et al. N Engl J Med. 1997;337:949–955.
Overgaard M, et al. Acta Oncol. 2007;46:533–551.

treatment: Prostate-bed RT + short-term ADT + pelvic nodal RT vs prostate-bed RT alone
population: 1,716 eligible men with PSA persistence or biochemical recurrence after prostatectomy
relativeEffect: 0.50 for pelvic nodal RT + ADT vs prostate-bed RT alone
benefitText: At 5 years, freedom from progression was 87.4% with prostate-bed RT plus short-term ADT and pelvic nodal RT versus 70.9% with prostate-bed RT alone, an absolute improvement of 16.5 percentage points (NNT 7). Adding ADT to prostate-bed RT alone produced an intermediate 81.3% rate. Acute grade 2+ toxicity was 44.6% vs 19.7% with pelvic nodal treatment, so the benefit comes with greater short-term toxicity.
clinicalQuestion: Does adding short-term ADT and pelvic nodal RT improve freedom from progression after prostatectomy salvage RT?

treatment: Adjuvant pembrolizumab vs placebo after nephrectomy
population: 994 patients with high-risk clear-cell RCC after nephrectomy, with or without completely resected metastases
benefitText: At 24 months, disease-free survival was 77.3% with pembrolizumab versus 68.1% with placebo, an absolute benefit of 9.2 percentage points (NNT 11). Overall survival at 24 months was 96.6% vs 93.5%. Grade 3+ adverse events were 32.4% vs 17.7%.
clinicalQuestion: Does adjuvant pembrolizumab improve disease-free and overall survival after nephrectomy for high-risk clear-cell RCC?
refs: Choueiri TK, et al. N Engl J Med. 2021;385:683–694.
Powles T, et al. N Engl J Med. 2024;390:1359–1371.

treatment: Adjuvant sunitinib vs placebo after nephrectomy
population: 615 patients with high-risk clear-cell RCC after nephrectomy
benefitText: At 5 years, disease-free survival was 59.3% with sunitinib versus 51.3% with placebo, an absolute benefit of 8 percentage points (NNT 13). Median DFS was 6.8 vs 5.6 years. The DFS benefit came with substantial toxicity and treatment discontinuation.
clinicalQuestion: Does adjuvant sunitinib improve disease-free survival after nephrectomy in high-risk clear-cell RCC?
refs: Ravaud A, et al. N Engl J Med. 2016;375:2246–2254.

treatment: Adjuvant nivolumab + ipilimumab vs placebo after nephrectomy
population: 816 patients with localized RCC at high risk of recurrence after nephrectomy
benefitText: At 24 months, disease-free survival was 76% with nivolumab plus ipilimumab versus 74% with placebo, an absolute difference of only 2 percentage points (NNT 50). The primary DFS endpoint was not met. Grade 3–5 adverse events were 38% vs 10%, and treatment discontinuation was 32% vs 2%.
clinicalQuestion: Does adjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab improve disease-free survival after nephrectomy for high-risk RCC?

treatment: Immediate adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy vs deferred chemotherapy at relapse
population: 284 patients with pT3–pT4 and/or N+ M0 urothelial carcinoma after radical cystectomy
benefitText: Immediate chemotherapy increased 5-year progression-free survival from 31.8% to 47.6%, an absolute improvement of 15.8 points (NNT 7). Overall survival was not significantly improved: 5-year OS 53.6% vs 47.7%, HR 0.78, P=.13. The trial closed early and was underpowered for OS.
nnH: Not applicable; toxicity comparisons are confounded by more patients receiving deferred treatment at relapse
clinicalQuestion: Does immediate adjuvant chemotherapy improve outcomes compared with deferred chemotherapy after radical cystectomy?
refs: Sternberg CN, et al. Lancet Oncol. 2015;16:76–86.

population: 28 patients with T3/T4, N1–N3 or M1 cisplatin-advanced penile carcinoma
benefitText: Irinotecan plus cisplatin produced 8 responses among 26 eligible patients, an objective response rate of 30.8%. The study was designed to exclude a response rate below 30% but did not demonstrate that threshold statistically. There were 3 grade 3 diarrhoeas and 2 grade 4 neutropenic fevers. NNT is not applicable because this was single-arm.
clinicalQuestion: Can irinotecan plus cisplatin produce clinically meaningful responses in locally advanced or metastatic penile cancer?
refs: Pizzocaro G, et al. Ann Oncol. 2008;19:1304–1307.

treatment: Three cycles BEP vs four cycles (3 BEP + 1 EP)
population: 812 men with good-prognosis metastatic germ-cell cancer
benefitText: Three cycles of BEP produced a projected 2-year PFS of 90.4% versus 89.4% with four cycles, a 1-point difference. The trial was designed to rule out a clinically important loss of efficacy and established three cycles as sufficient for good-prognosis disease. Three cycles also reduced treatment burden. NNT is not appropriate for an equivalence comparison.
nnH: Not quantifiable from the primary endpoint; fewer cycles improved several short-term quality-of-life measures
clinicalQuestion: Can three cycles of BEP provide equivalent disease control to four cycles in good-prognosis metastatic germ-cell cancer while reducing treatment burden?
refs: de Wit R, et al. J Clin Oncol. 2001;19:1629–1640.

treatment: Definitive SABR: 26 Gy single fraction for ≤4 cm tumours or 42 Gy in 3 fractions for >4–10 cm tumours
population: 70 patients with biopsy-confirmed primary RCC who were medically inoperable, high surgical risk or declined surgery
ci: Primary endpoint met; prespecified threshold was 90%
benefitText: FASTRACK II achieved 100% local control at 12 months in 70 treated patients, exceeding the prespecified 90% target. Median follow-up in the primary publication was 43 months. Grade 3 toxicity occurred in fewer than 10% of patients and there were no grade 4–5 events. This was a single-arm phase II study, so no comparative NNT can be assigned.
clinicalQuestion: Can stereotactic ablative body radiotherapy provide effective definitive local control for primary RCC in patients unsuitable for surgery?
refs: Siva S, et al. Lancet Oncol. 2024;25:308–316.
